sentences.text: In Sweden, you can become prime minister without a single yes vote.
Who can vote? Swedish citizens from 18, even abroad. Foreign residents vote locally, not for parliament.
Each party has its own ballot paper, yellow for parliament. Pick yours, mark one candidate if you like, and seal it in an envelope.
Votes fill the Riksdag, the parliament: 349 members who make laws and set the budget.
A party needs 4% nationwide, and 39 top-up seats make seats match votes.
Then parliament's Speaker, not the King, picks a prime minister, who's in unless 175 members vote no.
The King is head of state, but has no political power. He doesn't even sign laws.
In 2022, four parties on the right won 176 seats, and Ulf Kristersson got the job.
In 2026, the Speaker's first pick was voted down.
Should a prime minister need a yes vote, not just avoid a no?
